text:
Alice: Hey @support, our app is getting 401 invalid_api_key only when running from Vercel Serverless. Local curl works fine. Can we escalate? :confused:
Sam: Hi Alice — can you paste a minimal repro? 401 and only from Vercel sounds like the Authorization header might be getting stripped on redirect or by an edge proxy.
Alice: Repro below. curl -> 200, node fetch -> 401. We call https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

Alice: curl that succeeds:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX" "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Alice: node fetch fails:
```
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_live_XXXXX', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'hi' })
});
console.log(res.status); // 401
```

Sam: Thanks. Two quick checks — can you show the response headers from the failing request (including any 3xx status) and confirm the exact Node version on Vercel?

Alice: Node 18.x on Vercel. Here's the raw response headers we logged from the fetch attempt:
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
location: https://api.redwood.example.com/us-east-1/v1/generate
x-edge: cf-something
set-cookie: ...
```

Alice: Then follow redirect -> 401. curl followed redirect and preserved auth (on my laptop).

Sam: Interesting — by spec browsers and some fetch implementations drop Authorization when following cross-origin redirects for security. Also some runtimes on serverless platforms perform the redirect internally and do not propagate custom headers to the redirected request. That would explain curl vs runtime difference.

Sam: @Priya can you weigh in if we have any redirect rules from the global domain to region endpoints that would cause a 302?

Priya: Looking at our infra: we do global -> regional routing for latency (we 302 to nearest region on the root host if path misses region). We should not do that for API requests that may carry auth. This is an oversight. The redirect is what's dropping the header in the Vercel fetch follow.

Priya: Quick repro from our side replicates: node-fetch will do a 302 and the redirected request is unauthenticated -> 401. curl by default follows and will resend Authorization for same-origin redirects but not always for cross-origin. There's variance across clients.

Sam: Short term workaround for the customer: call the regional endpoint directly (we returned the Location header above) or set the fetch/axios to not automatically follow redirects and then re-issue the request to the Location with the Authorization header (manual follow). Example with node-fetch:
```
// manual redirect handling
const r = await fetch(url, { redirect: 'manual', headers });
if (r.status === 302) {
  const loc = r.headers.get('location');
  await fetch(loc, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
}
```

Alice: Ok we'll try hitting the long region URL for now. Can you fix server-side? This will hit many customers when running on serverless providers.

Priya: Filed infra ticket RINF-4821 to change routing to use a 307 (preserves method and should preserve Authorization behavior better) or ideally proxy internally so the client never sees a redirect. I've attached logs and the minimal failing script.

deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/redirect-fix branch (sha: abcd1234) :rocket:

Sam: Thanks @Priya. Alice — once the infra change rolls out (tracked RINF-4821) you should be able to go back to calling the global host. In the meantime, using the resolved region endpoint or manual redirect handling is the workaround.

Alice: Awesome, thanks for the quick turnaround. Will validate on Vercel and update here. :thumbsup:

Sam: Marking this resolved for the support thread; we'll post updates when RINF-4821 has rolled out.

Alice: Confirmed — region URL works, no more 401. Leaving this thread open until deploy-bot shows the fix rolled.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded for infra/redirect-fix (sha: abcd1234), rollout complete

Priya: Rollout done. We now proxy region routing instead of 302 redirect so Authorization headers won't be lost.

Alice: Verified in staging and production — global host works again. Thanks everyone! :party:
